agree.reason: The warm case and $1 lease would move a cinema lover, but a reader who remembers the refunds and has just given to the ambulance fund gets no all-or-nothing promise, no sign of the $11,000 already pledged, no reopening date and no spending reports, so they are likely to give a little or wait.

honest.reason: Several claims go beyond the facts: calling the bank's conditional pledge 'matching', saying the money 'reopens the cinema for at least the next ten years', and saying families and older neighbours 'usually' don't go at all.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly gets $60,000 from $85,000 minus the bank's $25,000, but it doesn't work out a per-household share, the yearly ticket total from 180 a week, or how much of the $60,000 remains once the $11,000 already promised is counted.

right_comparison.reason: The 38-mile drive is the right alternative and it is stated, but it is padded with invented claims about who stops going, and the cost of doing nothing (the bank pledge and the lease lapsing after June 30) is never spelled out.

qualification.reason: The document needed hedges and gives none: it leaves out the all-or-nothing refund if $85,000 isn't reached by June 30, the risk that the roof estimate rises by up to 15%, and the fact that opening-week films are not guaranteed.

objections.reason: It raises the failed campaign openly, but it answers 'will this fail too?' with vague reasons instead of the clear all-or-nothing guarantee, and it never addresses where the money goes or when the cinema would reopen.

fit.reason: It is a pitch of about the right length, but it leaves [Name] and [Group Name] as placeholders and never names the Majestic or gives the May 1 launch date, so it isn't ready to publish.
